did_you_know.text: Did you know? In this chapter, the LORD commands Samuel to stop mourning for Saul and anoint a new king from among Jesse’s sons, a man from Bethlehem.
Did you know? Samuel fears that Saul will kill him if he hears about the anointing, so the LORD tells him to take a heifer and present his visit as going to offer a sacrifice to the LORD.
Did you know? Before the sacrifice, Samuel consecrates Jesse and his sons and invites them to join him, so the gathering in Bethlehem takes place in the setting of a sacrifice.
Did you know? When Samuel is impressed by Eliab’s appearance and height, the LORD teaches him that people look at outward appearances, but the LORD looks at the heart.
Did you know? Jesse presents seven of his sons to Samuel, but Samuel declares that the LORD has not chosen any of them.
Did you know? David, the youngest son, is not initially present with the family but is out tending the sheep; only after Samuel asks about him does Jesse bring him in.
Did you know? Samuel anoints David in the presence of his brothers, and from that day onward the Spirit of the LORD comes powerfully upon him.
Did you know? The chapter describes a corresponding change involving Saul and David: the Spirit of the LORD departs from Saul, while it comes powerfully upon David after his anointing.
Did you know? David is described not only as a skilled musician, but also as a brave warrior, a man of wisdom in speech, and a handsome man; the text adds that the LORD is with him.
Did you know? When David plays the lyre, Saul finds relief: the evil spirit leaves him, and he feels better.
